author: Soulcall
quote:
This is the magnum opus of the GTA Series. 

By far the most alive feeling world, best protagonist, best physics. It has it all.

Everytime you replay this masterpiece, you don't enter it feeling all "man this game is dead feeling"

It feels ALIVE each time you start it back up. 

The soundtrack and story is a literal masterpiece 

This game is so good they brought back Niko in VI and for the moments he is on screen, he completely mogs the new characters and makes them feel like Temu GTA Protagonists.

author: Soulcall
quote:
This game is not GTA. This game is clearly marketed towards the Parasocial archetype in society who are chronically online. You can thank the GTA RP crowd for this slop. The story is nothing like a GTA Story. It is a relationship-situationship simulator. You are a errand boy for some woman that makes poor life choices, and acts like a child. The male character is berated for wanting to make smarter decisions. Toxic ex-girlfriend simulator. This is throughout the entire game.

The physics are wonky as hell because it is based on RDR2, and that game is while great, has very weighty and almost stiff movement. This does not work properly in GTA. Game is riddled with bugs. Game engine is still tied to Framerate in 2026, that is why it is locked to 30fps and probably why they are so many bugs. 

No way $2bn was spend on development, more like money laundering.

Game is blatantly racist towards only particular demographics (White, Asian) 

Glorifies "N@gg3r" and "304 culture"  

Game was made by social justice warriors and is marketed towards women.

author: Soulcall
quote:
Injected politics. Washed out visuals. No meaningful progression. Back to back worst maps in the series, so this one feels even worse than it actually is. 

The only thing they genuinely improved were some of the engine sounds, but even so, they lack low bass and proper gain. So even if you crank up your headphones or surround sound. The game just sounds weak compared to previous entries.

author: Soulcall
quote:
This game is so bad that it does not even deserve my time or effort into writing this review.

GameFreak/Nintendo has completely lost all credibility, and they have obviously lost their own way.

Pokemon is a far-cry and shadow of it's former self. I will not be buying anymore Pokemon products from this day forward. Simple as that.

author: Soulcall
quote:
This is the beginning of the truly bad trends. Poorly rendered environments. Annoying characters and companions. Extremely short and uninspiring story. Battle Scenes are atrocious. Camera is zoomed way too far in in most areas. Overly bright exposure in a lot of areas.

Lackluster pokemon roster, they just dump old gen on you and it kind of ruins the game.

Mega evolutions while cool, make the game E-Z mode, you need hacks to make it challenging. 

The integration of the Poke-Mart into the Pokemon Center is not a welcoming change. 

The overworld design and map layout is bad, confusing. Lumiose city controls is some of the worst programming I think I've seen.

Gym leaders have 3 weak pokemon. Just horrible balancing in general.

I wanted to like this game but that is just the reality.

author: Soulcall
quote:
This game was developed by a team who didn't know anything about Pokemon and managed to do a better job than what current developers can push out. 

It does suffer a bit from age, things like geometry on the pokemon models aren't the best thing to look at, but it has it's own charm.

I was fortunate to play these games on release and had the hardware to interact with my Gameboy games. You truly can't have known what it's like unless you lived it. 

Under a modern scope, this game has some glaring issues, but at the time, it was awesome spin-off and change from the traditional experience. 

While still following the traditional formula. It also was way more challenging than the main-line games. Which is what I enjoyed the game the most for, besides it's more open 3D world. 

This is how I honestly thought pokemon games were going to end up looking like on handhelds in the future, but boy is the future disappointing.

This is exactly how Pokemon should be crafted today but obviously with way better graphics and features. More pokemon etc. 

Not this sad excuse for "open world" we have today.

There is a mis-communication happening between the company and fans, and shareholders are manipulating the series into whatever genre is most popular. IE, "open world" 

Pokemon cannot be truly open world, it needs to have it's artistic hand-crafted levels that fully immerse you and make you feel like it's a different place from where you just where.

In the new games, everywhere feels the same.

But it's not all of them, and they have grown on me over the years.When the story, world-building and etc are so well done in the way they are, you can overlook that much much easier anyway.This storyline is better than Gen 4 storyline by quite a bit to me.

author: Soulcall
quote:
The reviews of this are way too overcritical and these people need to guide their hatred towards the CURRENT games coming out now which don't follow the actual Pokemon formula whatsoever.

Seriously, what timeline is this?? 

This game is not even that bad. Yeah I wish they had just remade Platinum, but i still did enjoy this game. It is a relatively faithful remaster of Gen 4.

The visuals do kind of leave more to be desired, the artstyle looks a bit more like Let's Go than it does Diamond and Pearl. Even so though, somehow things like the battle scenes and backgrounds are better animated than current games today. 

So what is the issue there that people even have?? If it's anything other than the general artstyle, then they are making things up. 

This isn't much different than how ORAS handled Gen 3, just a bit more limited, which, that's how D/P actually was. 

You don't see people review bombing ORAS because it didn't have the Battle Frontier and a bunch of features from Emerald.

author: Soulcall
quote: Obviously not the same RPG experience as something like FR/LG but this game manages to do many things right, mostly on the visuals side of things. It does capture some of that Gen 1 nostalgia and I can see it being a good entry for a kid just now growing up with pokemon, but it does have glaring **** Pokemon Go integration should have been scrapped entirely and they should've went full-bore on a Gen 1 reboot/remake. It is so close to capturing the essence of FR/LG, you can see it. They really missed a opportunity with this one. It's still a worthwhile play if you love Gen 1 and want some Nostalgia. It just doesn't have the same battle mechanics for wild pokemon (Works like Pokemon Go)Trainer battles are traditional but the environments actually look good in this game, even when compared to some later entries. Mega Evolutions are a cool addition.

author: Soulcall
quote:
This might be the best racing game of all time FOR it's time period. It gets hard to pin some of these above others. 
The sounds, the aesthetic(with Jeremy Clarkson), the progression, the visuals, cockpit view was unmatched, the handling. Fujimi Kaido. This game made me good at drifting in virtually EVERY other racing game, or reduced the learning curve. It also helped me memorize Sebring for track days. Thousands of hours spent online drag racing the Sebring straight.   *Chefs kiss*

author: Soulcall
quote: Best MC title by far. Most fleshed out and has the best visuals. Extremely satisfying handling and sense of speed. The customization is actually fun because the game looks good and there are accurate car models. It has a couple flaws but no need to mention them. You experience them, and move on because it's an amazing game. Spent thousands of hours online.

author: Soulcall
quote: Oddly enough I feel that Midnight Club LA is the best MC title. I did enjoy the original 2, but something about this game I just don't like. The graphics and the handling are pretty jarring to me. Especially compared to other games at the time.

author: Soulcall
quote: 9/10 because tire screech, car sounds were bad, the handling model leaves more to be desired, a bit on rails. The visuals were a bit weak too but that's the PS2's fault. Photomode is beautiful and on a emulator it's pretty mindblowing that it COULD look like that. GT3 is one of mine as well too. I started on GT but I think FM4 edges both of them out in the GOAT conversation. I also think GT3 had a better Aesthetic than both of those games but GT4/FM4 have a equal one.
